budget.metric: relative error of the coolant-dependent quantity (tool-work interface temperature rise above ambient, cutting force) under the case's coolant; chip grades are classifications (class match)
budget.note: Set after a first run of the coolant_reach harness had been seen (first-round report); justified only by the evidence below. The references are the same kinds of measurement as tool_temperature (tool-work thermocouple) and the main cutting force, so their budget (15 % of the rise, 15 % of the force) is carried over. The coolant effect itself is of that size (temperature drops of 11-27 % against dry in Sultana 2023), so this budget is only just discriminating: a model that ignored the coolant could pass where the effect is small, which the report states per case.

Set 16 of Ducobu et al. 2017 Table 1 (Seo, Min & Yang 2005, SHPB up to 1273 K and 1400 1/s), which Ducobu et al. recommend after comparing 20 sets in a CEL orthogonal-cutting model against experiments (best cutting force, mid-range feed force and chip thickness). Alternatives in the same table: Lee & Lin 1998 (782.7, 498.4, n 0.28, C 0.028, m 1, eps0 1e-5), Johnson 1985 (862.5, 331.2, 0.34, 0.012, 0.8), Meyer & Kleponis 2001 (896, 656, 0.5, 0.0128, 0.8), Kay 2002 (1098, 1092, 0.93, 0.014, 1.1). klippel-2024-ck45-orthogonal fitted A 867, B 344, n 0.361, C 0.0145 to their own bar (Table 9). Cross-check: lesuer-2001-llnl-jc (Table 1) use the Johnson 1985 set (862, 331, 0.34, 0.012, 0.8) for AMS 4911 plate, with JC damage constants D1 -0.09, D2 0.25, D3 -0.5, D4 0.014, D5 3.87 (not stored: they belong to another strength set). the Lee & Lin 1998 original was not readable (paywalled); its constants above are as quoted by Ducobu et al.

rule: tolerance = max(budget_pct/100 x |reference| (for temperatures: x the rise above ambient), 2 x the reference's uncertainty); a case passes when every compared value lies within its tolerance; a quantity passes when at least 80 % of its cases pass and no case misses by more than twice its tolerance
